messages:
jen: Deployed 3.4.1 to canary (us-west-2). Deploy-bot just posted a flag: p95 memory +40% vs baseline after ~10min. Not seeing errors but memory climbs. Should we let it roll or trigger auto-rollback?

deploy-bot: [automated alert] Canary deployment 3.4.1 -> memory_p95: +40% (10m). Threshold breach = true. Suggestion: trigger autorevert unless human override within 5m. See runbook: https://go/runbooks/canary-memory

matt: Hm. Any obvious correlation with the new tokenizer change? I remember we toggled chunked-prefix-cache in this build.

jen: yes chunked-prefix-cache enabled for embeddings route. But this is traffic hitting text-gen canary. Not the same route, could be unrelated. I want to avoid a noisy autorevert if ops can confirm.

ops-oncall: I'm pulling metrics now. Also seeing a small increase in CPU for the inference pods, but OOMs = 0. No restarts yet. p99 latency stable.

jen: ok plan proposal: hold automated rollback (manual override), pin canary to 3.4.1 blocked from progressing to staged, open a release-hold note, and do a controlled manual rollback to 3.4.0 if we still see degradation after 15m of observation. @sara can you draft a short customer-facing note in case we need a customer-facing rollback? :thinking_face:

sara: On it. Drafting: "We observed elevated memory usage on a canary deployment and are holding the rollout while we investigate. No customer impact observed at this time. We'll update within 30 minutes." Will post to #status if we escalate.

matt: For the manual rollback path, ops, can you run the rollback command if we hit another threshold? Command I propose: `deployctl rollback --env canary --service inference --to-version 3.4.0 --reason "memory_p95_regression"`

ops-oncall: confirmed. I'll watch the alert window. If memory_p95 remains >25% above baseline at 15m, I'll run your command and also pin traffic to 0% for 3.4.1. I'll leave a short note in the release ticket.

jen: Good. I'll update release notes on the internal doc: add an entry under "hold due to memory regression observed in canary" and mark the release window as BLOCKED. Also I'm toggling the deploy-bot override to prevent autorevert for 20m so humans can triage.

deploy-bot: [action] Autorevert suppressed by jen for 20m. Autorevert resume ETA: +20m.

ops-oncall: Watching. If we need to execute rollback I'll call it out here and post the `kubectl rollout undo` logs.

jen: Thanks everyone. If rollback executed, sara please prepare the release-note append: what changed in 3.4.1, why we rolled, and mitigation. If we don't rollback, we'll still patch the chunked-prefix-cache flag in next patch.

sara: Roger. Will have initial customer note ready in 10m and a full postmortem template if we end up reverting. :white_check_mark:
